title: Vitamin D Improves Depression in Liver Patients
brief_summary: This study evaluates the efficacy of vitamin D replacement therapy in reducing depressive symptoms in patients with chronic liver disease and vitamin D deficiency. Patients with normal vitamin D levels will be monitored as controls, and they will not receive any intervention.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* men and women
* over 18 years of age
* chronic liver disease

Exclusion Criteria:

* severe hepatic encephalopathy (CFF \<35 Hz)
* Interferon treatment
* hypercalcaemia (\>2.7 mmol/l) or hypercalciuria (\>8.0 mmol/d) with or without hyperparathyroidism (\>65.0 pg/ml)
* history of calcium-containing kidney stones
* allergy or hypersensitivity to any of the supplement ingredients: peanuts, soy, gelatin
* sarcoidosis
* stage IV or V Chronic Kidney Disease
* Pregnancy
